payload.body: Vectorization decision (2026-02-18): v1 retrieval uses local qmd embeddings/search with bindle-level archived memory candidates only, active-context exclusion enforced, and top-3 pre-response hooks. Reference clone: /Users/rabsef-bicrym/Development/tools/qmd (origin: git@github.com:tobi/qmd.git).

Vector policy lock (v1): keep retrieval simple and standard. Use one embedding per persisted memory object (turn/leaf/bindle/bindle_stub), no custom aggregation math, no synthetic centroid rollups in ranking path. Query against archived/off-context bindle artifacts only, enforce active-context exclusion before return, and return top-3 cues with summary_id pointers for expansion.

Implementation constraint: retrieval quality path uses real qmd embeddings on recall artifacts; do not introduce bespoke vector combination formulas in v1. If coarse routing is added later, gate it behind config and keep default off.
Hook contract: pre-response cues are produced from off-context retrieval only, topK=3 default, and each cue must include stable pointer IDs for sub-agent expansion.

Implemented Dolt schema/migration primitives for summary level/type metadata, archive lineage pointers, and qmd retrieval mapping fields. Added idempotent backfill for legacy leaf/condensed rows, new db helpers for lineage traversal/off-context metadata, and mirrored multi-tenant schema bootstrapping. Added/updated tests in summary/context suites for level/type mapping and lineage metadata APIs. payload.description:
# Objective
Deliver a dual-mode LCM runtime in Volt where either `dolt` (bounded lane model) or `upward` (recursive Josh-style condensation) can be selected by environment configuration, without behavior bleed between modes.

# Product Contract
- This is a first-class product requirement, not an experiment.
- Both modes must run in the same codebase and be selectable per-session by config.
- Strategy implementations must remain isolated so one mode cannot silently fall back to the other.
- Existing Dolt behavior remains valid unless explicitly changed by this epic.

# Required Outcomes
1. Unified naming/model contract for summary hierarchy:
   - Basal level: `leaf`.
   - Above leaf: ordered condensations (`d1`, `d2`, ..., `dn`).
   - Dolt terminology (`sprig`, `bindle`) remains presentation aliases over order levels, not a separate data model.
2. Shared pressure/fanout policy primitives for both modes, all env-configurable.
3. `/compact` dispatches to mode-specific compaction logic:
   - Dolt: short bindle behavior + bounded eviction rules.
   - Upward: same minimum grouping constraints, recursively compact upward, no eviction.
4. Ghost cues must be mode-scoped:
   - Enabled for Dolt behavior.
   - Disabled for Upward behavior.
5. Prompt selection must be mode-aware from a prompt registry/file layout.
6. Retrieval tools present one user-facing contract with mode-aware backend implementation.

# Non-Goals
- Rewriting non-LCM memory systems.
- Introducing partial hybrid mode semantics that blur Dolt and Upward behavior.
- Adding backwards-compatibility shims that preserve legacy ambiguous naming.

# Acceptance Criteria
- There is a single config switch selecting `dolt` vs `upward`.
- Strategy dispatch is explicit and tested; no implicit fallback.
- All subtask acceptance tests pass locally.
- Regression matrix covers pressure handling + manual `/compact` in both modes.
- README/docs describe mode selection and behavior differences.
payload.title: Dual-mode LCM runtime: Dolt + Upward strategy cutover

payload.description:
# Scope
Define and implement the canonical hierarchy contract used by both modes:
- `leaf` is the only basal unit.
- All summary levels above leaf are ordered condensations (`d1`, `d2`, `d3`, ...).
- Dolt names (`sprig`, `bindle`) become aliases/presentation labels only.

# Build Contract
1. Introduce a canonical internal representation for level/order that both strategies consume.
2. Ensure persistence can represent arbitrary condensation order for Upward while preserving Dolt semantics at `d1` and `d2`.
3. Remove ambiguous mixed naming from decision logic paths (naming may remain in user-facing display strings if mapped deterministically).
4. Add explicit conversion helpers for:
   - storage <-> canonical order representation
   - canonical order <-> display labels (`sprig`/`bindle`) where needed

# Constraints
- No silent normalization spread across call sites; conversion must be centralized.
- No compatibility shim that permits undefined level names.
- Migration must preserve existing rows and lineage references.

# Acceptance Tests
- Unit tests prove deterministic mapping for `leaf`, `d1`, `d2`, `dN`.
- Existing Dolt rows still load with expected labels.
- Upward mode can persist and read `d3+` without schema hacks.
- Regression test fails if an unknown level label reaches compaction logic.
payload.title: LCM taxonomy cutover: leaf + ordered condensation levels

payload.description:
# Scope
Create a shared policy engine and env-configurable contract used by both `dolt` and `upward` modes.

# Build Contract
1. Define shared policy primitives per level:
   - `target_tokens`
   - `hysteresis_tokens`
   - `min_fanout` (minimum items to roll up, must allow enforcing >=2)
2. Default values must match current Dolt sane defaults and be reused for Upward unless overridden.
3. Add env var parsing/validation for all policy fields and mode selection.
4. Fail fast on invalid policy values (negative thresholds, zero hysteresis where disallowed, min_fanout < 2 when level requires grouping).
5. Expose typed policy object to both strategies through one API.

# Constraints
- Do not duplicate separate policy codepaths that diverge over time.
- Keep runtime hot path free from ad hoc env lookups; parse once, pass typed config.

# Acceptance Tests
- Config tests cover defaults, overrides, and invalid inputs.
- Both strategies read the same parsed policy object shape.
- Regression test proves Dolt defaults remain unchanged when no new env vars are set.
payload.title: Shared pressure/fanout policy engine with env-configurable mode settings

payload.description:
# Scope
Introduce a strict strategy boundary so `dolt` and `upward` implementations are isolated behind one runtime contract.

# Build Contract
1. Define a strategy interface that includes at minimum:
   - threshold compaction entrypoint
   - manual `/compact` entrypoint
   - context assembly hooks
   - retrieval hook registration points
2. Move current Dolt runtime calls behind this interface without changing behavior.
3. Add mode-based strategy selection at session startup from typed config.
4. Emit explicit telemetry/log field containing active strategy name on compaction and manual compact events.

# Constraints
- No fallback to a default strategy if requested mode is unknown; startup must fail with clear error.
- No large `if (mode)` branching in central runtime after interface is introduced.

# Acceptance Tests
- Integration test shows requested mode dispatches to matching strategy implementation.
- Negative test fails startup on invalid mode string.
- Existing Dolt tests continue passing with interface-based dispatch.
payload.title: Strategy runtime boundary: mode-dispatched LCM interface and wiring

payload.description:
# Scope
Add Upward strategy (Josh-style) with recursive condensation semantics, sharing policy primitives and minimum grouping constraints from Dolt defaults.

# Build Contract
1. Implement Upward compaction flow:
   - roll lower order into next higher order using minimum fanout >= 2
   - recursively continue to higher orders while pressure remains and legal groups exist
   - never evict summaries off-context as part of Upward strategy
2. Upward manual `/compact` must mirror hard-limit style behavior:
   - force progression using the same grouping rules
   - still respect minimum fanout (no single-item condensation groups)
3. Keep live tail protection behavior aligned with shared runtime constraints.

# Constraints
- No ghost cue production in Upward mode.
- No fallback to Dolt-specific eviction behavior.

# Acceptance Tests
- Pressure simulation test verifies recursive level growth (`d1` to `dN`) under sustained pressure.
- Manual `/compact` test verifies upward compaction occurs and does not evict.
- Test asserts zero single-item condensations when min fanout is 2.
payload.title: Upward strategy implementation: recursive condensation without eviction

# Scope
Enforce ghost cue behavior as Dolt-only functionality with explicit guardrails to prevent accidental execution in Upward mode.

# Build Contract
1. Gate ghost cue generation and insertion behind mode check and config.
2. Dolt mode behavior remains as currently designed:
   - emit short narrative cue for evicted bindles/off-context summaries
   - include minimal machine-readable identifier front-matter where already required
3. Upward mode must never emit ghost cues.
4. Emit observability signal when ghost cue path is skipped due to mode.

# Constraints
- Do not rely on prompt-level instruction to suppress cues; suppression must be runtime logic.
- No hidden side effects (db writes, context inserts) for ghost cues in Upward mode.

# Acceptance Tests
- Dolt-mode test verifies cue generation on qualifying eviction.
- Upward-mode test verifies zero cue generation under equivalent pressure.
- Regression test asserts no ghost cue prompt load in Upward mode path.

payload.description:
# Scope
Unify manual `/compact` command semantics across modes with explicit strategy-specific behavior and user-visible outcome reporting.

# Build Contract
1. `/compact` must dispatch through strategy interface, not direct Dolt path.
2. Behavior by mode:
   - Dolt: short bindling workflow (roll older leaves while preserving tail, package sprigs, optional bounded bindle eviction).
   - Upward: force recursive condensation upward, no eviction.
3. When compaction is not viable (minimum fanout not met), return explicit no-op status to UI/TUI.
4. Ensure command output indicates which strategy ran and whether any compaction step executed.

# Constraints
- No silent no-op behavior.
- No strategy bypass in CLI command wiring.

# Acceptance Tests
- Command integration test for Dolt mode verifies short-bindle steps and status output.
- Command integration test for Upward mode verifies recursive compaction path and status output.
- No-op case test verifies explicit UI notice is emitted.

Canonical hierarchy:

- `d1` = first-order condensation of leaves.
- `d2` = second-order condensation of d1.
- `d3+` = higher-order condensations used by Upward mode.

Dolt presentation aliases:
- `d1` displays as `sprig`
- `d2` displays as `bindle`

# Build Contract
1. Introduce a canonical internal representation for condensation order that both strategies consume.
2. Replace fixed summary level naming with an order-based representation for summary rows:
   - add `condensation_order` (integer, >= 1)
   - migrate existing rows: `sprig -> d1 (order 1)`, `bindle -> d2 (order 2)`
   - keep `summary_type` for behavioral distinctions (e.g. `archive_stub`), but do not use it as a level system.
3. Keep leaves as message/turn-group entities, not summaries; do not create synthetic leaf summary rows.
4. Add centralized conversion helpers:
   - storage <-> canonical order
   - canonical order <-> display labels (`sprig`/`bindle`) for Dolt UX
5. Remove ambiguous mixed level naming from compaction decision logic.

# Constraints
- No silent normalization scattered across call sites; conversion must be centralized.
- No compatibility shim that accepts undefined level names/orders.
- Migration must preserve existing rows, lineage pointers, and retrieval behavior.

# Acceptance Tests
- Unit tests prove deterministic mapping for leaf, d1, d2, dN.
- Migration test confirms legacy `sprig/bindle` rows map to order 1/2 correctly.
- Upward mode can persist/read d3+ orders.
- Regression test fails if unknown level label/order reaches compaction logic.

# Scope
Create a shared policy engine and env-configurable contract used by both `dolt` and `upward` modes.

# Build Contract
1. Define shared policy primitives per condensation lane:
   - `soft`
   - `delta` (hysteresis band)
   - `target`
   - `min_fanout` (minimum roll-up group size, must allow enforcing >= 2)
2. Default values must match current Dolt behavior and become Upward defaults unless explicitly overridden.
3. Add typed env parsing/validation for mode selection and policy values (parse once at startup, inject typed config).
4. Fail fast on invalid policy values:
   - negative thresholds
   - `delta <= 0` for any lane
   - `min_fanout < 2` for condensation lanes
5. Expose one typed policy object consumed by both strategy implementations.

# Required Defaults (Current Dolt Baseline)
- `VOLTCODE_LCM_DOLT_LEAVES_SOFT = 50000`
- `VOLTCODE_LCM_DOLT_LEAVES_DELTA = 5000`
- `VOLTCODE_LCM_DOLT_LEAVES_TARGET = 50000`
- `VOLTCODE_LCM_DOLT_LEAVES_CAP = 50000`
- `VOLTCODE_LCM_DOLT_LEAVES_FRESH_TAIL_FLOOR = 4`
- `VOLTCODE_LCM_DOLT_SPRIGS_SOFT = 10000`
- `VOLTCODE_LCM_DOLT_SPRIGS_DELTA = 2000`
- `VOLTCODE_LCM_DOLT_SPRIGS_TARGET = 10000`
- `VOLTCODE_LCM_DOLT_BINDLES_SOFT = 10000`
- `VOLTCODE_LCM_DOLT_BINDLES_DELTA = 2000`
- `VOLTCODE_LCM_DOLT_BINDLES_TARGET = 10000`
- `VOLTCODE_LCM_DOLT_HARD_LIMIT_RISK_BUFFER = 0`
- `DEFAULT_CTX_CUTOFF_THRESHOLD = 0.6`
- `TARGET_FREE_PERCENTAGE = 0.25`
- `MIN_MESSAGES_TO_SUMMARIZE = 3`
- `MIN_LEAVES_PER_SPRIG = 2`
- `MIN_PROTECTED_TAIL_LEAVES = 2`
- `CRITICAL_THRESHOLD_MULTIPLIER = 1.2`
- `MAX_COMPACTION_ROUNDS = 10`
- summary/condense max output tokens = 2200

# Constraints
- Do not duplicate divergent policy evaluators per mode.
- Do not read env vars ad hoc in compaction loops.

# Acceptance Tests
- Config tests cover defaults, overrides, and invalid inputs.
- Both strategies receive the same typed policy object shape.
- Regression tests prove no behavior change when env overrides are absent.

# Scope
Introduce a strict strategy boundary so `dolt` and `upward` implementations are isolated behind one runtime contract.

# Build Contract
1. Define a concrete strategy interface with these methods:
   - `compactOnThreshold(input)` -> compaction result when soft-threshold/lane pressure is exceeded.
   - `compactManual(input)` -> `/compact` execution path.
   - `assembleContext(conversationID)` -> ordered context elements for prompt construction.
   - `resolveRetrieval(input)` -> mode-aware retrieval resolution.
2. Move these existing call sites behind the interface:
   - threshold compaction dispatch currently centered on `LcmContext.onContextThresholdReached`
   - manual compact dispatch from CLI/session compact command
   - context assembly currently using `getSummariesInContext` + `getMessagesInContext`
   - retrieval dispatch currently using `LcmRetrieval` entrypoints
3. Add mode-based strategy selection at session startup via typed config.
4. Emit telemetry/log fields with active strategy name for threshold and manual compaction events.

# Scope Boundary
Shared utilities that remain mode-agnostic:
- summarizer/condense LLM call wrappers
- database query/update primitives
- token accounting and budget calculation utilities

# Constraints
- Unknown mode must fail startup with explicit error (no implicit fallback).
- After interface introduction, central runtime should not accumulate large `if(mode)` branches.

# Acceptance Tests
- Integration tests prove configured mode dispatches to the correct strategy.
- Negative test proves invalid mode prevents startup.
- Existing Dolt behavior tests stay green through interface dispatch.

# Scope
Implement the Dolt strategy adapter under the new strategy interface with no semantic drift from current Dolt behavior.

# Build Contract
1. Port current Dolt behavior from the real active path (`LcmContext.onContextThresholdReached` and related helpers), not from `SessionCompaction` stubs.
2. Preserve lane behavior:
   - leaves lane compaction into d1/sprig
   - d1/sprig compaction into d2/bindle
   - hysteresis behavior and hard-limit bypass semantics
   - bindle eviction and off-context handling
3. Preserve ordering invariant in active context:
   - `<0..n bindles> <0..n sprigs> <0..n leaves>`
4. Keep existing thresholds/minimums unless changed through the shared policy config task.

# Constraints
- Behavior-preserving extraction only; no redesign in this task.
- Do not introduce new Dolt lane semantics.

# Acceptance Tests
- Existing Dolt compaction/context tests remain green.
- Invariant test verifies ordering after threshold compaction and manual `/compact`.
- Seeded fixture comparison shows equivalent output pre/post strategy extraction.

# Scope
Implement Upward strategy (Josh-style) with recursive higher-order condensation and no eviction.

# Build Contract
1. Implement recursive compaction from lower order to next order:
   - d1 -> d2 -> d3 -> ... while pressure remains and legal groups exist.
   - enforce `min_fanout >= 2` at every condensation step.
2. Upward condensation must support parent summaries above d1:
   - relax/parameterize the current Dolt-only invariant that restricts condensation parents to sprigs.
   - preserve Dolt invariant behavior when running Dolt strategy.
3. Manual `/compact` in Upward mode must run forced recursive compaction:
   - ignore soft-threshold gate for command invocation
   - perform at least one legal pass if possible
   - continue until no legal condensation group exists.
4. Never evict summaries off-context in Upward mode.
5. Keep live-tail protection aligned with shared runtime requirements.

# Constraints
- No ghost cue generation in Upward mode.
- No fallback to Dolt eviction behavior.

# Acceptance Tests
- Pressure simulation verifies dN growth under sustained pressure.
- Manual `/compact` test verifies forced recursive compaction and no eviction.
- Test fails if any single-item condensation group is created when fanout minimum is 2.

# Scope
Create a prompt registry/folder structure for mode-aware summarization/condensation with deterministic prompt selection.

# Build Contract
1. Establish prompt layout by mode + operation + order where applicable.
2. Prompt resolution API must select prompt by active mode and requested operation.
3. Keep token control split:
   - target range guidance in prompt text
   - hard output cap (`max_output_tokens`) at API call site
4. Remove references to old prompt escalation variants by name:
   - normal -> aggressive -> deterministic truncation
   and replace with single prompt variants per mode/operation.
5. Registry naming must follow canonical taxonomy from `volt-dc7.1`.

# Constraints
- No hardcoded inline prompt bodies in compaction logic.
- Missing prompt mapping/file must fail explicitly (no silent default fallback).

# Acceptance Tests
- Unit tests cover prompt resolution for both modes.
- Failure test for missing prompt mapping.
- Summarization tests assert `max_output_tokens` is applied at call sites.

# Scope
Unify retrieval behind one user-facing contract while allowing mode-specific backend resolution.

# Build Contract
1. Keep existing user-facing retrieval entrypoints stable (including `lcm_expand_query`) and avoid mode-specific user commands.
2. Introduce a retrieval adapter selected by active mode.
3. Retrieval behavior by mode:
   - Dolt mode: support off-context archive lookup + lineage traversal.
   - Upward mode: no off-context eviction path; off-context retrieval returns explicit diagnostic/no-result, while in-context expansion/search traverses active condensation DAG.
4. Keep response shape stable across modes so callers do not branch on mode.
5. Document backend differences and diagnostics in tool/API help text.

# Constraints
- Do not silently drop resolvable lineage.
- Do not introduce new public tool names in this task.

# Acceptance Tests
- Integration tests for shared retrieval entrypoints in both modes.
- `lcm_expand_query` returns meaningful mode-appropriate results in both modes.
- Explicit test verifies Upward off-context retrieval emits diagnostic/no-result contract.

# Scope
Enforce ghost cue generation as Dolt-only functionality with hard runtime guardrails.

# Build Contract
1. Gate ghost cue generation/insertion behind active strategy mode and config.
2. Dolt mode behavior remains current:
   - generate short narrative cue for evicted bindles/off-context summaries
   - include machine-readable bindle identifier front-matter where required.
3. Upward mode must never generate ghost cues.
4. Emit telemetry/event when ghost cue path is skipped due to mode.

# Constraints
- Suppression must be runtime logic, not prompt text convention.
- Upward mode must perform no ghost-cue side effects (no prompt load, no DB write, no context insert).

# Acceptance Tests
- Dolt test verifies cue generation on qualifying eviction.
- Upward test verifies zero cue generation under equivalent pressure.
- Regression test verifies ghost cue prompt is never loaded in Upward mode path.

# Scope
Unify manual `/compact` semantics behind strategy dispatch with explicit user-visible status output.

# Build Contract
1. `/compact` must dispatch through strategy interface (no direct Dolt bypass).
2. Behavior by mode:
   - Dolt: run existing workflow explicitly:
     - compact oldest leaves beyond protected tail into d1/sprig summaries
     - compact sprigs into bindles when eligible
     - if bindles exceed target, perform bounded eviction + ghost cue (Dolt only)
   - Upward: run forced recursive condensation to higher orders until no legal group remains; no eviction.
3. If no legal compaction group exists (fanout constraints), return explicit no-op status.
4. UI/TUI output must include active strategy and whether compaction executed.

# Constraints
- No silent no-op behavior.
- No strategy bypass in CLI command wiring.

# Acceptance Tests
- Dolt command integration test verifies expected sequence + status output.
- Upward command integration test verifies forced recursive path + status output.
- No-op scenario test verifies explicit user notice.

# Scope
Add full cross-mode regression matrix and operator documentation for dual-mode LCM operation.

# Build Contract
1. Implement cross-mode test matrix covering:
   - pressure-triggered compaction
   - manual `/compact`
   - retrieval behavior
   - ghost cue gating
   - context ordering and live-tail preservation
2. Add deterministic seeded fixtures for comparable Dolt vs Upward runs.
3. Update operator docs in `packages/voltcode/README.md` with:
   - mode selection env vars
   - pressure/hysteresis/minimum tuning env vars
   - behavioral invariants and differences by mode
   - troubleshooting for mode misconfiguration.

# Constraints
- Documentation must match actual env var names/defaults.
- Tests must fail if mode selection silently falls back.

# Acceptance Tests
- CI path includes cross-mode tests and passes locally.
- `packages/voltcode/README.md` includes a dedicated dual-mode section with runnable examples.
- Negative config test proves invalid mode causes startup failure.

Fixes identified during code review (self-review + independent Codex review) of the
fix/lcm-inline-content-path-resolution branch before merge to dev.

The branch introduces lcm_read (a tool that lets models retrieve large content stored
in LCM by file ID) and fixes the storage model for inline payloads. The core feature
works and was verified E2E, but review surfaced 9 discrete issues ranging from type
safety holes to a high-severity multi-tenant migration gap.

These subtasks are ordered by dependency. The upgrade refactor revert (C6) is
independent and will be handled by the coordinator. All others are delegated to
Codex workers.
payload.title: PR review fixes for lcm-inline-content-path-resolution

## Problem

The array ["lcm_expand", "lcm_grep", "lcm_read"] is defined as a const inside TWO
separate component functions in packages/voltcode/src/cli/cmd/tui/routes/session/index.tsx:

1. Inside AssistantMessage (line ~1559)
2. Inside ToolPart (line ~1837)

If a new LCM tool is added, both must be updated or the UI silently breaks for one
rendering path. This is a DRY violation.

## Required change

1. Extract `LCM_INTERNAL_TOOLS` to a single module-level const, defined once near the
   top of session/index.tsx (or in a shared constants file if one exists nearby).
2. Replace both inline definitions with references to the shared const.
3. At each usage site, add a brief comment: // See LCM_INTERNAL_TOOLS definition above
   (or the import path if extracted to a separate file).

## Scope boundaries

- Do NOT refactor anything else in session/index.tsx.
- Do NOT change the contents of the array — only where it's defined.
- Do NOT move the component functions or change their signatures.

## Acceptance criteria

- grep -c "LCM_INTERNAL_TOOLS" on session/index.tsx shows exactly 1 definition
  and 2+ references (not 2 definitions).
- The TUI still renders correctly (typecheck passes, no runtime change).

## Problem

packages/voltcode/src/tool/lcm-read.ts defines:

    interface LcmReadMetadata {
      fileId: string
      found: boolean
      truncated: boolean
      totalSize: number
      storageKind?: string    // <-- THIS
    }

The successful return path (lines 129-140) never populates storageKind. It is always
undefined at runtime. This is dead surface area that confuses future readers into
thinking the field carries meaningful data.

The storageKind is not surfaced to the model (metadata goes to the processor, not
the model's context), so there is no value in returning it.

## Required change

Remove the `storageKind?: string` line from the LcmReadMetadata interface.

## Scope boundaries

- Do NOT add storageKind population logic. We're removing the field, not fixing it.
- Do NOT change any other interface or type in the file.

## Acceptance criteria

- LcmReadMetadata has exactly 4 fields: fileId, found, truncated, totalSize.
- Typecheck passes.

payload.description:
## Problem

lcm_read signals the processor to skip re-storage by setting metadata.lcm = { storedInLcm: true, fileId }.
The processor reads this at processor.ts:534 via toolResult.metadata?.lcm?.storedInLcm.

But:
- LcmReadMetadata (lcm-read.ts:23-29) does NOT include an lcm field.
- The processor accesses it through TypeScript's structural typing / any escape.
- If Tool.define's metadata generic is ever tightened, this breaks silently at runtime
  with no compile-time error.

## Context: how Tool.define metadata works

Look at packages/voltcode/src/tool/tool.ts to understand the Tool.define<P, M> generic.
The second type parameter M is the metadata type. The processor receives toolResult.metadata
typed as whatever M is. Right now it's loose enough that extra fields sneak through, but
that's an accident of the current type system, not a contract.

## Required change

1. Define a shared type in a sensible location (e.g. packages/voltcode/src/session/lcm/types.ts
   or alongside the existing LCM types — use your judgment):

       export interface LcmToolMetadata {
         storedInLcm: boolean
         fileId: string
       }

2. Update LcmReadMetadata in lcm-read.ts to include:

       lcm?: LcmToolMetadata

3. Update processor.ts to import and use LcmToolMetadata for the type of lcmMetadata,
   rather than relying on any/structural typing. The access pattern
   toolResult.metadata?.lcm?.storedInLcm should be type-safe after this change.

4. If other LCM tools (lcm_expand, lcm_describe, lcm_grep) also set metadata.lcm,
   update them too. If they don't, leave them alone.

## Scope boundaries

- Do NOT change the runtime behavior. The same values flow through the same paths.
  This is purely a type-safety improvement.
- Do NOT refactor the processor's large-output handling logic.
- Do NOT add new metadata fields beyond what already exists.

## Acceptance criteria

- toolResult.metadata?.lcm?.storedInLcm access in processor.ts is fully typed
  (no any, no structural escape).
- LcmReadMetadata includes lcm?: LcmToolMetadata.
- Typecheck passes with no new suppressions or casts.
- The shared type is importable from a single canonical location.
payload.title: Type the metadata.lcm escape hatch between lcm_read and processor

payload.description:
## Problem

packages/voltcode/src/session/lcm/db.ts lines 2019-2031 contain a backward-compatibility
fallback in getLargeFileContent:

    // Backward-compatibility fallback for rows that predate storage_kind enforcement.
    if (row.original_path) {
      const file = Bun.file(row.original_path)
      const exists = await file.exists()
      if (!exists) {
        log.warn("legacy large file path not found on disk", { fileId, path: row.original_path })
        return null
      }
      const content = await file.text()
      return { content, truncated: false, totalSize: content.length }
    }

This code:
1. Ignores the maxBytes parameter entirely (reads full file into memory).
2. Always returns truncated: false regardless of actual size.
3. Is unreachable after the migration runs (the migration backfills storage_kind
   on ALL existing rows, so the code above this block always matches).

We want a clean cutover. No backward-compat shims.

## Required change

Delete the entire backward-compatibility fallback block (the if (row.original_path)
block that comes AFTER the storage_kind === "path" branch). The function should fall
through to `return null` after the path and inline_text branches.

Also delete the comment "Backward-compatibility fallback for rows that predate
storage_kind enforcement."

## Scope boundaries

- Do NOT modify the storage_kind === "path" branch above it (that one is correct
  and respects maxBytes).
- Do NOT modify the inline_text branch.
- Do NOT add any new fallback logic. If storage_kind is somehow unrecognized,
  returning null is correct.

## Acceptance criteria

- The backward-compat block is gone.
- getLargeFileContent has exactly three code paths: inline_text → return content,
  path → read from disk with maxBytes, everything else → return null.
- Typecheck passes.
payload.title: Delete backward-compat fallback in getLargeFileContent

payload.description:
## Problem

packages/voltcode/src/session/lcm/db.ts lines ~461-478 contain two separate DO blocks
for the large_files_storage_shape_check constraint:

Block 1 (DROP): Checks if constraint exists, drops it.
Block 2 (ADD): Adds constraint, catches duplicate_object.

If execution crashes between the DROP and ADD, the table is left without a constraint.
Additionally, every app startup unconditionally drops and recreates the constraint even
when nothing changed — that's a gratuitous write on every boot.

## Required change

Combine both operations into a single DO block so the DROP and ADD are atomic within
one PL/pgSQL execution. Also add a guard: only drop-and-recreate if the constraint
definition has actually changed.

Here's the pattern:

    DO \$\$ 
    DECLARE
      current_def text;
      desired_def text := '((storage_kind = ...))';  -- the full CHECK body
    BEGIN
      -- Get current constraint definition if it exists
      SELECT pg_get_constraintdef(oid) INTO current_def
      FROM pg_constraint
      WHERE conname = 'large_files_storage_shape_check'
        AND conrelid = 'large_files'::regclass;

      -- Only recreate if missing or changed
      IF current_def IS NULL OR current_def != desired_def THEN
        IF current_def IS NOT NULL THEN
          EXECUTE 'ALTER TABLE large_files DROP CONSTRAINT large_files_storage_shape_check';
        END IF;
        ALTER TABLE large_files
          ADD CONSTRAINT large_files_storage_shape_check CHECK (
            (storage_kind = 'path' AND original_path IS NOT NULL AND content IS NULL AND binary_content IS NULL) OR
            (storage_kind = 'inline_text' AND content IS NOT NULL AND binary_content IS NULL) OR
            (storage_kind = 'inline_binary' AND binary_content IS NOT NULL AND content IS NULL)
          );
      END IF;
    END \$\$;

NOTE: The desired_def string must match what pg_get_constraintdef returns for the
CHECK expression. You'll need to check the exact format PostgreSQL uses (it may
normalize parentheses, spacing, etc.). Test by running the migration, then querying
pg_get_constraintdef to see the canonical form, and use THAT as your comparison string.

If getting the exact string match is fiddly, an acceptable alternative is: just wrap
the DROP + ADD in a single DO block (so they're atomic) and skip the "has it changed"
optimization. Atomicity is the must-have; skip-if-unchanged is nice-to-have.

## Scope boundaries

- Only touch the CHECK constraint migration block.
- Do NOT modify the constraint definition itself.
- Do NOT change other migrations in the same file.

## Acceptance criteria

- The DROP and ADD are in a single DO block (atomic execution).
- Typecheck passes.
- If you can verify: running the migration twice in a row does not error.
payload.title: Make CHECK constraint migration atomic and idempotent

payload.description:
## Problem

packages/voltcode/src/tool/lcm-read.ts lines 16-20 define:

    max_bytes: z
      .number()
      .min(1)
      .optional()
      .describe("Optional byte limit for very large payloads (default: 100000)")

There is no .max() guard. A model could pass max_bytes: 999_999_999. The path-backed
branch in getLargeFileContent (db.ts) already has a 100MB safety cap:

    const safeMax = Math.min(maxBytes ?? 100 * 1024 * 1024, 100 * 1024 * 1024)

But the inline_text branch does not — it trusts maxBytes directly. Capping at the
Zod level makes the schema the single source of truth for the limit.

## Required change

Add .max(100_000_000) to the max_bytes Zod chain:

    max_bytes: z
      .number()
      .min(1)
      .max(100_000_000)
      .optional()
      .describe("Optional byte limit for very large payloads (default: 100000)")

100_000_000 (100MB) matches the existing safety cap in the path-backed branch.

## Scope boundaries

- Only change the Zod schema definition.
- Do NOT change the DEFAULT_MAX_BYTES constant (100_000) — that's the default,
  not the maximum.
- Do NOT modify getLargeFileContent.

## Acceptance criteria

- max_bytes has both .min(1) and .max(100_000_000).
- Typecheck passes.
payload.title: Cap max_bytes at 100MB in lcm_read Zod schema

payload.description:
## Problem (HIGH SEVERITY — identified by independent Codex review)

packages/voltcode/src/session/lcm/user-context.ts manages per-user PostgreSQL schemas
for multi-tenant cloud deployments. When a user schema is created, it runs
CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS for all LCM tables.

The storage_kind column was added to the public schema via ALTER TABLE migrations in
db.ts (lines ~433-478), including:
- ALTER TABLE large_files ADD COLUMN storage_kind text
- Backfill from existing data
- SET DEFAULT 'path'
- SET NOT NULL
- DROP NOT NULL on original_path
- ADD CHECK constraint

But user-context.ts has NONE of these migrations. Any existing user schema created
before this change will crash with "column storage_kind does not exist" when
lcm_describe or lcm_read queries hit SELECT ... storage_kind ... FROM large_files.

## Required change

In the ensureUserSchema function in user-context.ts, after the CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS
block for large_files, add the same migration steps that db.ts has:

1. ALTER TABLE large_files ADD COLUMN storage_kind text (wrapped in exception handler
   for duplicate_column)
2. Backfill: UPDATE large_files SET storage_kind = CASE WHEN content IS NOT NULL
   THEN 'inline_text' WHEN binary_content IS NOT NULL THEN 'inline_binary'
   ELSE 'path' END WHERE storage_kind IS NULL
3. ALTER COLUMN storage_kind SET DEFAULT 'path'
4. ALTER COLUMN storage_kind SET NOT NULL
5. ALTER COLUMN original_path DROP NOT NULL
6. The CHECK constraint (using the same atomic pattern from volt-66c if that's
   done first, otherwise the existing DROP+ADD pattern)

Also update the CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS statement for large_files in user-context.ts
to include storage_kind in the column list for NEW schemas, matching the definition
in db.ts.

## How to find the code

Look at ensureUserSchema in user-context.ts. It has a large SQL template string that
creates all LCM tables. Find the large_files CREATE TABLE and add migrations after it.

Then look at db.ts for the exact migration SQL to replicate.

## Scope boundaries

- Only modify user-context.ts.
- Mirror the migration logic from db.ts — do not invent new migration patterns.
- Do NOT modify db.ts itself.

## Acceptance criteria

- user-context.ts CREATE TABLE for large_files includes storage_kind column.
- ALTER TABLE migrations for storage_kind exist in ensureUserSchema.
- The backfill logic matches db.ts exactly.
- Typecheck passes.
payload.title: Add storage_kind migration to multi-tenant user schemas

payload.description:
## Problem (identified by independent Codex review)

getLargeFileContent in db.ts handles two storage_kind values explicitly:
- inline_text: returns content from the DB column
- path: reads from disk with maxBytes slicing

But inline_binary is never handled. The code falls through to the backward-compat
fallback (which we're deleting in volt-d7e), and then to return null.

When getLargeFileContent returns null for an inline_binary record, lcm_read.ts
checks largeFileExists (which returns true — the row exists), and then tells the
model: "File record exists but content could not be read — the backing file may
have been moved or deleted."

This is wrong. The file wasn't moved or deleted — it's a binary blob stored in the
DB. The error message is misleading.

## Required change

### In db.ts getLargeFileContent:

After the inline_text branch and before the path branch, add an inline_binary branch:

    if (row.storage_kind === "inline_binary") {
      // Binary content cannot be returned as text. Return null so the caller
      // can give an appropriate error message.
      return null
    }

This is a no-op for retrieval (we can't usefully return binary as text), but it
makes the control flow explicit.

### In lcm-read.ts:

Before the generic "backing file may have been moved" error, add a check for
binary content. You'll need to either:

(a) Have getLargeFileContent return a discriminated result that says WHY it's null
    (not found vs binary vs disk missing), OR

(b) Query getLargeFile (which returns the full row including storage_kind) and
    check storage_kind before giving the error message.

Option (b) is simpler. The code already calls largeFileExists when result is null.
Instead, call getLargeFile and check storage_kind:

    if (!result) {
      const file = await LcmDb.getLargeFile(fileId, conversationId ?? undefined)
      if (file) {
        if (file.storage_kind === "inline_binary") {
          return {
            title: `LCM read: ${fileId}`,
            metadata: { fileId, found: true, truncated: false, totalSize: 0 },
            output: `File "${fileId}" contains binary content (${file.mime_type}) which cannot be displayed as text.\n\nUse lcm_describe with "${fileId}" for metadata about this file.`,
          }
        }
        // Path-backed file whose disk content is missing
        return {
          title: `LCM read: ${fileId}`,
          metadata: { fileId, found: true, truncated: false, totalSize: 0 },
          output: `File record exists but content could not be read — the backing file may have been moved or deleted.\n\nUse lcm_describe with "${fileId}" for metadata and exploration summary.`,
        }
      }
      // Truly not found
      return { ... not found response ... }
    }

## Dependencies

This task depends on volt-d7e (delete backward-compat fallback), since that task
removes the code path that inline_binary currently falls through to.

## Scope boundaries

- Do NOT attempt to decode or display binary content.
- Do NOT change the inline_text or path branches in getLargeFileContent.
- Do NOT change lcm_describe behavior.

## Acceptance criteria

- An inline_binary record does NOT produce "backing file moved or deleted" error.
- An inline_binary record produces a clear message saying it's binary content.
- A path-backed record with missing disk file still produces the "moved or deleted" message.
- Typecheck passes.
payload.title: Handle inline_binary explicitly in getLargeFileContent and lcm_read

## Background

Commit 70a5534e0 ("refactor: replace upstream upgrade sources with voltropy install
script") was reverted from the fix/lcm-inline-content-path-resolution branch because
it was unrelated to the LCM bug fix. The commit is preserved in git history.

That commit did the right thing architecturally — it replaced ~170 lines of
package-manager sniffing (npm, brew, choco, scoop, pnpm, bun, yarn) and their
respective version-check endpoints (GitHub releases, npm registry, Homebrew formulae,
Chocolatey API, Scoop manifests) with a single install script and version endpoint.

But it pointed at Voltropy infrastructure (voltropy.com/install, api.voltropy.com).
Voltropy is handing the product off to Martian Engineering, so the endpoints need
to be updated before this lands.

## Required change

1. Cherry-pick 70a5534e0 onto a new branch (off dev, after the LCM fix merges).
2. Replace all Voltropy references with Martian Engineering equivalents:
   - `https://www.voltropy.com/install` → whatever the Martian Engineering install
     script URL will be
   - `https://api.voltropy.com/v1/bootstrap/download-url` → whatever the Martian
     Engineering version API will be
   - Any other voltropy.com references in the cherry-picked code
3. Update the env var from VOLT_VERSION to whatever is appropriate (check if the
   new install script expects the same var name).

## Open questions (must be answered before implementation)

- What are the Martian Engineering URLs for the install script and version API?
- Is the install script API-compatible with the Voltropy one, or does it need
  adaptation?
- Do we want to keep the "curl | sh" pattern or use something else?

## Reference

- Original commit: 70a5534e0
- View it: git show 70a5534e0
- Revert commit: b9e12ed5f (on fix/lcm-inline-content-path-resolution)

## Acceptance criteria

- Separate PR on its own branch, not bundled with anything else.
- All voltropy.com references replaced with Martian Engineering endpoints.
- The upgrade command works end-to-end (or is clearly marked as needing
  infrastructure that doesn't exist yet).
- Typecheck passes.

## Context

LongMemEval (https://github.com/xiaowu0162/LongMemEval) is a benchmark for
evaluating chat assistants on long-term interactive memory. Published at ICLR 2025.
Paper: "Benchmarking Chat Assistants on Long-Term Interactive Memory."

Volt's LCM (Lossless Context Management) is specifically designed to preserve and
retrieve context across long conversations — summaries, large file storage,
conversation ancestry. This benchmark is a natural fit for measuring how well
LCM actually performs at long-term recall.

## Required work

1. Read the LongMemEval repo and understand the evaluation protocol, task categories,
   and metrics.
2. Determine what adapter/harness is needed to run Volt against the benchmark.
3. Implement the adapter.
4. Run the eval and report results.

## Open questions

- What conversation lengths does the benchmark test? Does it exceed Volt's
  compaction thresholds?
- Does the benchmark require multi-session memory or single-session only?
- What are baseline scores for comparable systems?

## Reference

- Repo: https://github.com/xiaowu0162/LongMemEval
- Paper venue: ICLR 2025
payload.title: Run LongMemEval benchmark against Volt's LCM

payload.description:
## Background

GitHub issue #3: `nix build github:voltropy/volt#packages.x86_64-linux.voltcode` fails because `nix/node_modules.nix` line 32 includes `../install` in its fileset, but no top-level `install` file exists in the Volt repo. It was a top-level install script from the upstream OpenCode repo that didn't survive the fork (commit 944c7943c). Nix evaluates filesets strictly — a missing path is an immediate error.

Additionally, `flake.nix` exports a `desktop` package target that cannot build (the desktop app has its own broken references, tracked separately). Advertising it as a buildable target misleads users.

## Behavioral contract

1. Remove `../install` from the `lib.fileset.unions` list in `nix/node_modules.nix` (line 32).
2. Remove the `desktop` definition (line 42-44) and its export (line 65) from `flake.nix`, so `nix flake show` no longer advertises it as a buildable package.
3. Do NOT delete `nix/desktop.nix` or anything under `packages/desktop/` — the code stays, it's just not wired into Nix as a target.

## Scope boundaries

- This task does NOT fix the desktop app itself (the broken `include_str!` reference in `cli.rs`). That's a separate pebble.
- This task does NOT touch any non-Nix files.

## Acceptance criteria

- `../install` no longer appears in `nix/node_modules.nix`
- `desktop` no longer appears in `flake.nix` outputs
- `nix/desktop.nix` and `packages/desktop/` are untouched
- `bun typecheck` passes (sanity — these are Nix-only changes, but confirm no collateral)

Closes #3
payload.title: Remove stale ../install from Nix fileset and unexport desktop package

## Background

`packages/desktop/src-tauri/src/cli.rs` line 51 uses `include_str!("../../../../packages/volt-gateway/install.sh")` — a Rust compile-time macro that embeds a file's contents as a string literal. The referenced file `packages/volt-gateway/install.sh` does not exist in the Volt repo. It was part of the upstream OpenCode project and didn't survive the fork.

This means the desktop Tauri app cannot compile at all. The `include_str!` macro fails at build time.

The desktop app is not currently being built or shipped. This pebble exists to track the known breakage so it's documented, not to drive immediate action.

## What the code does

`install_cli()` in `cli.rs` writes the embedded install script to a temp file and runs it with `--binary <sidecar-path>` to symlink/copy the bundled CLI binary into `~/.voltcode/bin/volt`. It's the mechanism for the desktop app to install the CLI for terminal use.

## When this matters

Only if/when someone decides to revive the desktop app. At that point, the full desktop package needs an audit against post-fork changes — this broken reference is just one of potentially many issues.

## Scope

- This is a tracking pebble, not an implementation pebble
- No work is expected until the desktop app is prioritized
- volt-b5c (the Nix fix) removes the desktop target from flake.nix so nobody trips over this in the meantime
payload.title: Track broken desktop app build (stale install.sh reference)
